episode_title: EPISODE 9: Beyond the Search Bar – Andrew Holland on Why SEO Lost Its Credibility

real_qa.q: Why has demand for SEO agencies declined by 50% year on year?
real_qa.r: Demand for SEO agencies worldwide has reduced by 50% year on year due to confusion created by white hat SEO influencers who defensively claimed that SEO and GEO are the same thing. This triggered a civil war within the industry that made SEO appear uninvestable to CFOs and CMOs, combined with new metrics like AI visibility and citation visibility that lacked clear ROI compared to traditional traffic metrics.

real_qa.q: How should brands measure GEO success in early adoption when AI search is not yet stable?
real_qa.r: Brands must track whether they are being recommended by AI systems across multiple prompts over time, expecting daily changes in responses. The key is ensuring all content and marketing activities have real-world value at the moment of publication—whether that is improved landing pages, PR placements, YouTube presence, or email campaigns—rather than gambling on tactics purely for citation visibility.
real_qa.requete: measure GEO success AI search early phase

real_qa.q: What is the relationship between brand positioning and GEO recommendations in AI search results?
real_qa.r: GEO performance fundamentally comes down to how well-positioned a brand is in its market. Clients who are well-positioned appear consistently in AI responses for relevant prompts, while those who are not well-positioned or lack sufficient distribution fail to appear on broad prompts despite strong organic SEO performance. Positioning, copywriting, content marketing, PR, and third-party validation are the primary drivers.
real_qa.requete: brand positioning GEO AI search recommendations

real_qa.q: Why is SEO still valuable for businesses spending heavily on paid search?
real_qa.r: If a company is spending significant budget on paid search clicks for buyer intent terms but has no organic ranking presence for those same keywords after years of investment, SEO remains valuable to establish organic visibility and reduce paid search dependency. However, as AI search becomes more dominant, the value of traditional SEO will diminish because Google may shift to AI-based results.
real_qa.requete: SEO value paid search organic ranking

real_qa.q: What are the key differences between optimizing for Google search versus AI search engines?
real_qa.r: AI search has access to the entire internet, not just Google's index, plus personal user intelligence and internal reasoning capabilities. Unlike traditional SEO which optimized for page one ranking by satisficing (good enough), AI search evaluates content across multiple dimensions including positioning, brand distribution, and third-party validation. The shift requires marketing and PR expertise rather than purely technical SEO tactics.
real_qa.requete: AI search versus Google SEO optimization differences

guest.bio_context: Andrew Holland is a contrarian voice in the search marketing industry with data-driven perspectives on SEO and GEO trends. He has turned down multiple speaking engagements at industry conferences and serves as an influencer for SEO tool platforms, bringing a critical analysis to how the industry has responded to AI-driven search changes.
